fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Reading Rand Instead of Rumors", "body": "Gabe opened by relaying conspiracy world chatter about Ayn Rand, including questions about her gender and the symbolism of her book titles, while saying he kept being drawn to her work. Joel replied that such rumors came from people who never applied the reason Rand taught, and he contrasted those who followed breadcrumbs with those who read an 1100 page book for themselves. Yerasimos urged listeners to read Atlas Shrugged before judging her. One host called the truth community an echo chamber of interpretations of interpretations, and other speakers argued a philosopher should not be judged by later followers, citing Hegel and Nietzsche."}, {"title": "Altruism Versus Rational Self Interest", "body": "Yerasimos described the morality of collectivism as altruism, where anything done for others counted as good and anything done for oneself counted as evil. One of the guests argued that a person who had filled his own cup became more inclined and more able to help others, while a society conditioned to equate selflessness with virtue gave from empty cups, resentment and guilt. One host said that if everyone looked after themselves first, mass altruism would hardly be needed. A guest also stressed that rational selfishness meant honoring yourself, not getting one over on anyone."}, {"title": "Self Worth, Pricing, and Trade", "body": "Chance described how he learned to pay what people asked without seeking discounts, found that the universe returned as much or more, and tied self worth to the sacral center in his Biofield Tuning work. A guest answering him cited Rand's view that trade was the only rational ethical principle for human relationships and said a trader loved virtues rather than weaknesses. A guest suggested a trader focuses on giving as much value as possible. Another guest said beginners might work for free to gather testimonials and let the market set their price, while one host argued that charging by the hour was a false valuation tied to Chronos."}, {"title": "Reason, Introspection, and Know Thyself", "body": "One of the hosts read a passage on the maxim know thyself, which argued that absurdities arose when people forgot the limits of their senses, and the guests tied this to Rand's idea of reason as the application of the mind to reality. Yerasimos said introspection required time alone and reflection on how you acted in the world, and he warned that constant devices pulled people away from it. A guest read Rand on the rational faculty as the basis of survival and said humans alone could choose not to think. A guest added that compounding good decisions built authentic self esteem."}, {"title": "Fear, Dissonance, and Self Efficacy", "body": "Gabe suggested turning the maxim play to your strengths into honoring your strengths by pursuing your weaknesses and tackling your fears. Chance said dissonance was not evil but led to harmony when a person allowed and witnessed it, a lesson he said came to him through music and tuning forks. Joel described defending himself against public health order fines in New South Wales, said he won all three cases, and defined self efficacy as the willingness and ability to learn what is needed to meet life's challenges. Chance later added that suppressed anger could undermine self esteem."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Yerasimos Stilianessis and Joel Rafidi, the guys from Here For the Truth Podcast join Vibe Rant tonight! On the docket is the philosophy of Objectivism and the school of Ayn Rand, emphasizing the importance of self-esteem, reclaiming your heroic individuality, and more.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "This is going to be a conversation that I think breaks some spells on a lot of people's perceptions of a thinker in a school of philosophy that has been largely swept under the rug, if not outright demonized.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In my research today, I'm comparing her against Nietzsche and seeing the fine line between them. And it's a very important line to be aware of, because a lot of these philosophical conundrums can be taken a little too far in certain ways. And I think that's a nice line to draw out, the difference between atheism and nihilism completely.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Everything that I'm hearing now is actually a product of a lack of application of what Ayn Rand actually taught, which is reason, which is rationality, which is objectivity, which is the power of one's mind to actually navigate reality, which is to not grant oneself license to create illusions and myth-mongering simply because one does not know.", "author": "Joel Rafidi", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/86e485fa-459f-4f3a-9955-af979c2fff1d/JOEL-RAFIDI.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's going to be those people that listen to the breadcrumbs floating around, and there's going to be those people that actually dive deep into an 1100 page book and discover things for themselves. And there's a very distinct line between those two kinds of people.", "author": "Joel Rafidi", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/86e485fa-459f-4f3a-9955-af979c2fff1d/JOEL-RAFIDI.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Look at the world we're living in. Like Joel was saying, we're living in this arch collective society where anything that you do for anyone else and where you sacrifice yourself is considered good. And yet anything that you do for yourself is considered evil, which is pretty much the morality of collectivism, which is altruism.", "author": "Yerasimos Stilianessis", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/4e59decf-e436-4562-a3bd-b7d0cbe70fec/YERASIMOS-STILIANESSIS.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And when you truly love yourself and know yourself and make decisions that are in your rational self interest, you're more likely to achieve fulfillment and satisfaction in your life. And I can speak personally for myself. That's where I'm at.", "author": "Yerasimos Stilianessis", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/4e59decf-e436-4562-a3bd-b7d0cbe70fec/YERASIMOS-STILIANESSIS.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Don't ask for a discount. Don't even think twice about it. Just fearlessly be like, that's what it costs? I can pay that. Here it is, because it's what I need right now. It's what fits the equation. The more I do that, the more I find that the universe provides a return in some way that matches or exceeds what I just put in, in almost an instant turnaround.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Because the truth people, a lot of times the people in the truth community, they get so sucked into the rabbit holes. But are they happy? Are they fulfilled? Are they doing the things they want to do just because of what the evil ones are doing? Are you creating? Are you being productive?", "author": "Yerasimos Stilianessis", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/4e59decf-e436-4562-a3bd-b7d0cbe70fec/YERASIMOS-STILIANESSIS.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Now I'm loving the challenge of that phrase, play to your strengths. Maybe we could tweak these maxims, improve them, layer them and restructure them. Maybe it's honor your strengths by pursuing your weaknesses, or honor your strength by tackling your fears. It's not so much find what you're good at and go to what's comfortable. That's the stagnation mentality.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I have found that in all forms that it comes, dissonance is not evil. It is not to be avoided. It's actually there to lead you to harmony. If you go through the dissonance and you allow it and witness the dissonance, then harmony is the result.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And then years later, you get into the menu, and you're like, oh, I can't believe I had this setting set to that. That doesn't work at all. Now that I know how to use the camera, I can't believe that I totally just left it like that. It's been messing up my photos the whole time. The beliefs about who you used to be are just like that.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "What self-esteem tells you is that to have self-esteem, you have to have self-efficacy. And self-efficacy is the willingness and the ability to learn what you need to learn to deal with the challenges of life. So if I don't know the answers, how can I go discover the answers?", "author": "Joel Rafidi", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/86e485fa-459f-4f3a-9955-af979c2fff1d/JOEL-RAFIDI.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
